chunk_map.heading: ## Read the sharpen with a skeptical eye

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Sequential read holds: 'the side quest' (chunk 5, L45) resolves to the exercise titled 'Open the side quest' named in chunk 4 (L33); 'm3-security'/'m3-quality' windows are self-named on first use (chunk 5, L45/47); 'the map'/'loop' (chunk 6, L65) are arc-earned spine vocabulary per the carve-out. No unresolved pronoun or forward-only referent found outside the carve-outs.

grep -n 'said\|earlier module\|previous module\|the opening lecture' on the expanded body returned nothing. All cross-module references name the module by number (M1/M2/M4) or by exercise/lecture title, never by position.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 2 (L10-12) references 'the feature you planned at M2' and 'you noted the path at M2 close'. Verified against curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/plan-mode-done-right.md L79/L85/L170: that file's close beat has the student note the plan-file path and a task, explicitly cross-referencing earn-the-trust.md by quote in its artefact-contract table. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal demo beat pattern in this file (no 'guess before you watch/see' construction).

Every chunk (1-11) carries at least one self-carrying claim or a real navigational payload (Start here's include links, Pre-read's dated Willison pointer, Next's two-signature close). None is a bare wait-state bullet.

Checked each non-canonical header against its chunk body: 'Sharpen the skill from evidence' (L43) matches the skill-rewrite + rules-integration content; 'Read the sharpen with a skeptical eye' (L61) matches the caveats/opt-up content; 'Clear the session' (L69) matches the wrap prompts. No header contradicted by its own chunk.

Checked each sub-item: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction (only a single isolated 'Not a quarter-long epic' at L14, not the triple-negation shape); no anaphora/epistrophe triples found; no self-grading superlative about the module/exercise (Key Concepts L92 'worth more than a perfect generic one' is a general claim about codebase-tuned skills, not self-praise of this training); no number-plus-retraction; no abstraction-noun stacks; no empty-leg verb triplets.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -niE 'beat|mood|compendium|forcing function|firing|surface as|writing surface|Connections\b' over the body (lines 1-114) returned one hit at L58, which sits inside the fenced Prompt block (L53-59, exempt). 'the surface you're most nervous about' (L31) and 'the access surface' (L91) use 'surface' as the ordinary security term-of-art this module teaches (access surface / attack surface), not the repo's writing-surface dialect. 'slop-sharing' (L94) is not on the banned-term list.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm the rule prevents: full-sentence bold reads as decorative shouting rather than marking a retrievable handle, flattening the visual hierarchy a room-scale reader relies on to find the one term worth grabbing. Harm present here: yes, on two chunks. Chunk 2 'Prework' L14: '**A feature you could ship in a few hours. Not a quarter-long epic.**' bolds a full two-sentence directive (13 words), not a <=5-word handle. Chunk 9 'Bring to Module 4' L99: '**One scoped task you'd send off rather than nudge bit by bit: a real slice. Bigger than a typo-fix, smaller than an epic.**' bolds a ~24-word multi-sentence span. Neither section is a reading-list/menu or lookup surface (the only carve-out that lifts the per-slide budget), so the whole-sentence-bold ceiling applies at full strength. (What You'll Learn's L22-27 single-word verb leads — Fork/Invoke/Split/Author/Test/Ship — are within the handle pattern and not flagged.)
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Bold only the handle inside each sentence (e.g. 'a few hours' / 'a real slice'), leave the rest of the sentence plain.
